title: What the tax roll shows after the public bought
question: After each purchase, did the building leave the tax roll as public property does, was it exempted, and does the roll show it changing hands again?
finding: Of 41 purchases with a roll history, 35 went off the tax roll as government property, most on the first or second roll after the Board file; 4 are too recent to see. In 2 the site was divided and part of it still carries an assessed value: 333-12th Street ($1,137,827 on the latest roll); 1500-1580 Mission Street ($410,110,178 on the latest roll). 1 still carried a value on two or more yearly valuations after the file before leaving the roll (450 Sixth Street). The rolls show a further sale date after the one that records the public purchase for 1: 921 Howard Street (30 March 2021). The two hotels a nonprofit bought stayed on the roll under a welfare exemption.
how: For each purchase, every roll whose valuation date (1 January of the roll year) falls after the Board file was read: status code N with no land or improvement value is how the roll marks government property; the class code and exemption are those on the latest roll; a sale date later than the one that records the public purchase is listed as a further transfer.
limits: The roll shows status, not owners or deeds. A building that stays on the roll may be owned by a nonprofit or a housing partnership on City land, which is the design of most subsidised housing; a further sale date may be a transfer between the City and its housing partner, a ground lease, or a lot being divided, none of which the roll tells apart. The roll records no price. The value that appears after a sale date is an indicator of the price, because California law re-sets assessed value to the price paid when a property changes hands; exemptions, a transfer of part of a property, transfers the law excludes from reassessment and new construction all break that link. The recorded deed and its transfer-tax declaration at the Assessor-Recorder would settle what was paid; neither is open data. Purchases made after 1 January 2025 are too recent for any roll on the portal.
